paragraphs.text: A cash-secured put involves a writer setting aside enough cash to purchase shares at the strike price should the put be assigned. The writer initially sells the put, collecting a premium, and accepts the obligation to buy one hundred shares per contract at the specified strike price before expiration [S1]. Assignment is the mechanism through which an option writer is required to meet an obligation when a contract holder exercises their right [S2]. LEAPS, or Long-term Equity AnticiPation Securities, are listed options with an expiration date greater than one year, allowing investors to gain long exposure to a stock with less capital than outright purchase [S3].

An option premium is composed of intrinsic value and extrinsic value, which is also called time value. Intrinsic value measures how much the option is currently 'in the money,' whereas extrinsic value is the remainder of the premium. For an out-of-the-money option, the premium represents pure extrinsic value [S4].
